line: Young nigga that’s runnin’ ’bout all ’em apes no I ’ain’t Tarzan If I can get ’em my squad can
vault_lines: Young nigga that's runnin' 'bout all 'em apes no I 'ain't Tarzan
meaning:
They got gangstas on that side, It’s savages on this side

Making a comparison between his squad and actual apes, G Herbo claims to run with savages! Real dangerous folk who are willing and ready to wild out out at any given moment. He also makes a reference towards the 1999 film, Tarzan, whose main protagonist is raised by gorillaz.

line: Yeah my name hold weight that’s what my bars say
vault_lines: Yeah my name hold weight that's what my bars say
meaning: Literally and metaphorically, Herb’s bars provide a great example for his come up in the Drill scene. Perhaps referring to bars of gold bars or something implying heaviness, a lot of weight basically. Of course the mention to his real “bars” refers to all of the words and lines he spits when rapping.

line: Yo boyfriend a zero, I’m rollin’ off a hero, yo baby-mama she deep-throat
vault_lines: Yo boyfriend a zero, I'm rollin' off a hero, yo baby-mama she deep-throat
meaning:
Agreeing and paying homage to Tink’s chorus where she says:

Yo nigga a zero
Self-made bitch, I don’t need no fuckin' hero

Bibby also acknowledges the people who throw hate towards him and his squad, referring to this female’s significant other as a “zero” as a quick comeback.

His “hero” in this case would be the drugs that get him incredibly high, hence the words “I’m rollin' off”. And to add even more insult to injury, the mother of your child is providing Bibby with some great top!

line: I be goin’ hard no time off, these lil’ niggas they rhyme soft Play with me I let the nine off, commit a homicide then ride off
vault_lines: I be goin' hard no time off, these lil' niggas they rhyme soft
meaning:
Previous bars by Herb can relate to the same situation. From the track “Kill Shit”, which also happens to feature Bibby:

Know a couple niggas that’s down to ride for a homicide
When it’s drama time
Run up on a nigga with the llamas flyin
Leave his loved ones all traumatized

Bibby stays on his grind at all times. As well as having the desire to create music, his eagerness to make money hasn’t decreased one single bit over time. Therefore he always makes an attempt to rhyme harder than the next emcee, hence why other rappers “rhyme soft” compared to him.

Furthermore, Bibby isn’t fond of playing games when he’s all about business. Those willing to test his realness will regret choosing to do so – he’s always ready to bang at somebody who asks for it.

line: Weak bitches gon’ talk shit but a real bitch ain’t gon’ let it slide
vault_lines: Weak bitches gon' talk shit but a real bitch ain't gon' let it slide
meaning:
Legendary saying to live by suggested by rap phenomenon, JAY Z, from the song “Dirt Off Your Shoulders”:

Niggas is crazy baby, don’t forget that boy told you
Get, that, dirt off your shoulder

Fame and popularity have their weaknesses of course. The more successful and known Tink seems to become, the more people critique or hate on her career as an artist.

However, Tink suggests that the individuals that let all the hate consume them are weak minded. She on the other hand does not care for what others say or think about her or her music.

line: Got more toys than a spoiled brat, playin’ games that’ll get you clapped
vault_lines: Got more toys than a spoiled brat, playin' games that'll get you clapped
meaning:
Referring to “boy toys” here, Tink makes a comparison to the men she fools around with to the amount of actual toys that a privileged child would own.

To continue the kid friendly theme, she goes on mention the games she plays. Having a dangerous effect on her life and comparable to that of many Trap-Rappers now a days. Hence why she’s really good friends with both Herb and Bibby.

vault_lines: Runnin' shit like Nino, my plug named Carlito
meaning:
When you’re dealing drugs like Bibby you need a connect, who can supply you the drugs, in this case a guy called Carlito. Carlito is a name associated with a mexican/hispanic mate, he might insist that he is not only dealing locally but also internationally, accross the border.

It might also coincidentally refer to the movie “Carlito’s Way” directed by Brian de Palma.

line: Baby, I’m thuggin’, I can’t be your boyfriend
vault_lines: Baby, I'm thuggin', I can't be your boyfriend
meaning: Baby, I’m thuggin’, I can’t be your boyfriend

line: Tatted on me, we skin deep, and I ride with him, no DMV
vault_lines: Tatted on me, we skin deep, and I ride with him, no DMV
meaning: Tink uses a simile by comparing intercourse to the DMV (Department of Motor Vehicles) by saying she would “ride” someone during sexual intercourse, but she would also renew her license or tabs at the DMV, allowing her to legally “ride” in her vehicle.
